paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: when you come before God, listen first and talk less. The Teacher says to "Guard your steps" and to draw near to listen (Ecclesiastes 5:1). Why? Because "God is in heaven and you are on earth," so the Teacher says to let your words be few (Ecclesiastes 5:2).

Now, this isn't about God wanting a quiet room full of nervous people, because the Teacher is saying that a lot of words can't make up for a heart that isn't really listening. He says "as many dreams bring futility, so do many words" (Ecclesiastes 5:7). And I know that one personally, friend: I have given some LONG speeches to dough, and it STILL stayed dough!

So what do you do with your words? Mean them and keep them, because "It is better not to vow than to make a vow and not fulfill it" (Ecclesiastes 5:5), and if you do make a vow, "Fulfill your vow" (Ecclesiastes 5:4). Then the Teacher wraps it all up with three words: "Therefore, fear God" (Ecclesiastes 5:7). So today, baker, take it slow, listen close, and let every word you bring to God be a word you mean.
